Chapter 6: Moving from Awareness to Action.
Awareness is often that first spark—the moment when you suddenly see the world’s injustices with fresh eyes. But what happens after that spark? The real challenge comes later, in those quiet, everyday moments when you can actually do something... but taking action isn’t always easy, is it?
Imagine you’re at work, and there’s talk about a new policy. On the surface, the conversation is polite, but underneath, you can sense the tension. A few folks notice that, while the policy seems neutral, it’s probably going to make it harder for people from certain backgrounds to move ahead. Now, there’s a choice: do you speak up and risk some awkwardness, or do you stay quiet and let it slide by?
Most of us don’t realize just how often these moments pop up. Maybe it’s a joke that doesn’t quite land, a hiring decision that feels a bit off, or a meeting where only a few voices ever get heard. It’s easy to look away, hoping someone else will say what needs to be said. But every single time, the chance to act is right there.
For those who decide to speak up, something important becomes clear—being antiracist isn’t just about what you believe, it’s about what you’re willing to do. It means asking the hard questions, challenging old assumptions, and sometimes shaking up the status quo. Maybe you’re the only one in the room willing to call out an issue. Other times, it’s about having someone’s back when they take that risk.
And action doesn’t always have to be loud or dramatic. Sometimes, it’s a quiet word after a meeting. Maybe it’s suggesting the team take a closer look at a policy. Or it could mean joining with others to push for change, even when it’s not clear what’ll happen next. The important thing? Keep moving forward—choose action over silence, again and again.
Over time, these small steps start to add up. They help create a culture where fairness isn’t just a goal, it’s the expectation. Where people support each other. And where injustice finds it harder to slip by unnoticed. The work never really ends, and the path can be messy. But every step you take makes a difference.
